question: What was the capital of North-western province under Ashoka?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Taxila **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Taxila**

 
 
• **Taxila** was the capital of the **North-western province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• Located in present-day Pakistan, Taxila was a major center of learning, trade, and culture during ancient times.
 
• It served as a strategic administrative and military hub due to its location on important trade routes.
 
• Ashoka's inscriptions and policies, including the spread of Buddhism, were implemented in Taxila.
 
• The city's significance continued even after the Mauryan Empire, as it remained a prominent center for education and commerce.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ujjayini:**

 
 
• **Ujjayini** (modern-day Ujjain) was the capital of the **Western province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• It was an important city in ancient India, known for its cultural and religious significance.
 
• Ujjayini was a major center for trade and commerce, located on the trade routes connecting northern and southern India.
 
• It is not associated with the North-western province but played a crucial role in the administration of the Western region.
 
• The city is also mentioned in ancient texts like the Mahabharata and is associated with the legendary king Vikramaditya.
 
 
 
• **Tosali:**
 
 
• **Tosali** was the capital of the **Eastern province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• Located in present-day Odisha, Tosali was an important administrative center for the region.
 
• Ashoka's rock edicts and inscriptions have been found in this region, indicating its significance during his reign.
 
• Tosali was not associated with the North-western province but played a key role in the governance of the Eastern territories.
 
• The city's exact location is believed to be near modern-day Dhauli, where Ashoka's famous Dhauli Edict is located.
 
 
 
• **Suvarnagiri:**
 
 
• **Suvarnagiri** was the capital of the **Southern province** under Ashoka's Mauryan Empire.
 
• Its name translates to "Golden Mountain," and it was an important administrative and economic center.
 
• Suvarnagiri was located in present-day Karnataka and served as a hub for trade and resource management.
 
• It was not associated with the North-western province but was crucial for the administration of the Southern territories.
 
• The city's strategic location helped Ashoka maintain control over the southern regions of his empire.
